note: Implementation-specific evals (typing discipline and property-based testing) where this skill, not the companion concerns skill, is the primary driver. The cross-skill behavioural cases live under ../../coordinate-time-systems/evals/. Run with-skill vs baseline, ideally repository-denied.

evals.name: review-typed-api
evals.expected_output: Identifies each type-safety hole and gives the fix: bare Vector3 should be frame-tagged Vec3<F>; the blanket impl<F: Eci> using a raw vector lets an approximation propagate to future frames silently (use explicit per-frame impls); the Utc->Ut1 From assuming dUT1=0 is a silent EOP-free downgrade (require an EOP provider); the SimpleEci->Gcrs From is a silent precision upgrade that should not exist; era() belongs only on Epoch<Ut1>. Overall: make meaningful operations expressible and meaningless ones uncompilable.
expectations: Flags the bare Vector3<f64> position/acceleration types and recommends frame-tagging them (e.g. Vec3<F>) so frames cannot be mixed silently
Flags the blanket impl<F: Eci> over a precision-aware operation as letting an approximation propagate to future frames with no compile error, and recommends explicit per-frame impls
Flags the Epoch<Utc> -> Epoch<Ut1> conversion that assumes dUT1 = 0 and recommends requiring an EOP provider instead (no EOP-free UT1)
Flags the SimpleEci -> Gcrs conversion as a silent precision upgrade (approximate masquerading as rigorous) that should not be provided
Flags that era() is defined on Epoch<Utc> and should exist only on Epoch<Ut1> (ERA is a UT1 observable)
Frames the fix as making the meaningful operations expressible and the meaningless ones fail to compile (type the frame/scale; don't launder raw values on public APIs)

evals.name: proptest-rotation-scale
evals.prompt: We have a unit-quaternion `Rotation<From, To>` type (with `inverse`, composition, and `transform(Vec3<From>) -> Vec3<To>`) and a scale-tagged `Epoch<S>` with conversions (`to_tai`, `to_utc`, `to_tt`, ...). Write a property-based test plan using `proptest`: which invariants should hold, what must the input generators cover, and sketch the key tests.
evals.expected_output: Rotation round-trip (inverse(r) composed with r is identity) and magnitude preservation; composition associativity and identity; scale round-trip (utc->tai->utc) including a generator that lands on a leap-second boundary and a duration-across-boundary check; assert with an explicit tolerance, never == on a transformed f64; generators cover degenerate inputs (near-zero/parallel vectors, element singularities) and non-finite (NaN/+/-inf); quaternion unit-norm/renormalization (and/or covariance PSD) as an invariant.
expectations: Includes a rotation round-trip invariant (inverse(r) o r approximately identity) and magnitude preservation (|r.v| approximately |v|)
Includes composition invariants (associativity and/or r o inverse(r) approximately identity)
Includes a scale round-trip (e.g. utc->tai->utc) and explicitly exercises a leap-second boundary (duration across it)
Specifies asserting with an explicit tolerance, never == on a transformed f64
Says generators must cover degenerate inputs (near-zero/parallel vectors) and non-finite inputs (NaN/+/-inf)
Mentions quaternion unit-norm hygiene / renormalization (or covariance positive-semidefiniteness) as an invariant
